title: Rabbi David Tawil: Life Lessons From Pirke Abot- "Behavioral Momentum"

chapters.title: Physics and Behavioral Momentum
chapters.about: Defining momentum and how it applies to human behavior and habits.

chapters.title: Mitzvah Goreret Mitzvah
chapters.about: The Mishnaic concept that one Mitzvah leads to another.

chapters.title: The Negative Cycle
chapters.about: How one bad action can lead to a cycle of negative behavior.

chapters.title: Mitzvot in Parashat Ki Teitzei
chapters.about: Discussing the many Mitzvot in the Parasha including Eishes Yefat Toar.

chapters.title: Shiluach HaKen and Ma'akeh
chapters.about: The Mitzvot of sending away the mother bird and building a fence.

chapters.title: Preparing for Rosh Hashanah
chapters.about: Using Pat Yisrael as a tool to build momentum before the holidays.

summary: Rabbi Tawil explains the concept of behavioral momentum, where performing one positive deed or Mitzvah creates a mindset that makes it easier to perform subsequent good actions. He illustrates this through examples from daily life and the Torah, specifically discussing Mitzvot in Parashat Ki Teitzei and the practice of eating Pat Yisrael during the days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.
questions: How does doing one small Mitzvah lead to doing more?
Why does the Torah allow for certain behaviors like Eishes Yefat Toar if they are not ideal?
What is the purpose of eating Pat Yisrael during the ten days of repentance?
How can we build positive momentum in our daily lives?
